## Glyphling 0.9.1 (test build for 1.0)

Download `Glyphling-Setup-0.9.1.exe` below and run it. It updates an existing installation in place, keeping settings, themes and position.

### New
- **Automatic updates**: Glyphling checks the GitHub releases by itself, tells you once when a newer version exists and, when you agree, downloads the setup and installs it over the current copy. Settings > Info has a manual check and a switch to turn the automatic check off.
- **CPU temperature sensor, on request**: if no source is available, Settings offers to install LibreHardwareMonitor (downloaded from its official releases, started at logon through a scheduled task; Windows asks for administrator consent once). Nothing is installed without that button.
- **Music source**: the widget follows one app at a time (the one that is playing) and the circle's volume changes only that app, never the system volume. Pick the apps from a list of popular players, add your own, and use them as a whitelist or a blacklist.
- **Cover colors**: new switch to show the album cover in plain white instead of the theme colors.
- **Mode label** now moves below the circle when the widget is near the top, so the circle can sit closer to the top edge.
- The shake easter egg is much harder to trigger.

### Fixes
- Quick positions no longer push the circle (and its ring) off the screen.
- Settings never shows the standard Windows title bar, also when it loses focus.
- The disk picker lists your real drives (letter and name).
- Smoother panel opening: the window glide is time based and the blur filters are gone from the animation.

The setup is not signed yet: Windows SmartScreen may warn on first launch ("More info" → "Run anyway").
